subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A pure substance, unlike a mixture, will:
options: Melt and boil at specific sharp temperatures
Melt over a range of temperatures
questions.explain: A pure substance has a sharp, specific melting and boiling point, whereas mixtures melt and boil over a range.

questions.q: Which technique would best separate two coloured dyes in an ink?
questions.explain: Chromatography separates a mixture of soluble coloured substances by how far each travels.

questions.q: When sodium hydroxide is added to a solution of copper(II) ions, the precipitate is:
questions.explain: Copper(II) ions form a blue precipitate of copper hydroxide with sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: When silver nitrate solution is added to a chloride solution, the precipitate formed is:
questions.explain: Chloride ions form a white precipitate of silver chloride with silver nitrate.

questions.q: In chemistry, a formulation is best described as:
options: A useful mixture made in carefully measured quantities
questions.explain: A formulation is a mixture made to a precise recipe, such as paint or a medicine.

questions.q: Which technique would best separate a soluble solid from its solution to obtain crystals?
questions.explain: Crystallisation evaporates the solvent so the dissolved solid forms crystals.

questions.q: A white precipitate forms when barium chloride is added to a solution containing:
questions.explain: Sulfate ions form a white precipitate of barium sulfate with barium chloride.

questions.q: Oxygen gas can be identified because it:
questions.explain: Oxygen relights a glowing splint.

questions.q: Copper ions produce which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Copper ions give a green flame colour.

questions.q: When silver nitrate is added to a bromide solution, the precipitate formed is:
questions.explain: Bromide ions form a cream precipitate of silver bromide.

questions.q: To test for halide ions with silver nitrate, why is dilute nitric acid added first?
options: To remove carbonate ions that would also give a precipitate
To make the gas test work
questions.explain: Nitric acid removes carbonate ions so they don't form a precipitate and give a false halide result.

questions.q: Adding sodium hydroxide to iron(III) ions produces a precipitate that is:
questions.explain: Iron(III) ions give a brown precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide.

questions.q: Which test confirms that a gas is hydrogen?
options: It gives a squeaky pop with a lit splint
questions.explain: Hydrogen produces a squeaky pop when a lit splint is held to it.

questions.q: Potassium ions produce which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Potassium ions give a lilac flame colour.

questions.q: A substance that does not move from the baseline in chromatography is most likely:
questions.explain: A spot that stays on the baseline is insoluble in that solvent and does not travel.

questions.q: In paper chromatography, the Rf value is calculated as:
options: Distance moved by solvent - distance moved by substance
Distance moved by substance / distance moved by solvent
Distance moved by substance x distance moved by solvent
Distance moved by solvent / distance moved by substance
questions.explain: Rf = distance moved by the substance divided by the distance moved by the solvent.

questions.q: Flame emission spectroscopy works by measuring the:
options: Light given out when metal ions are heated in a flame
questions.explain: In flame emission spectroscopy, heated metal ions emit light with a pattern that identifies them.

questions.q: Chlorine gas is identified because it:
questions.explain: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper, turning it white.

questions.q: In a flame test, lithium ions give which colour?
questions.explain: Lithium ions produce a crimson flame.

questions.q: Which flame colour indicates the presence of sodium ions?
questions.explain: Sodium ions produce a yellow flame in a flame test.

questions.q: How can you test for the presence of carbonate ions?
options: Add silver nitrate to form a precipitate
Add acid and bubble the gas through limewater
questions.explain: Carbonates react with acid to release carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky.

questions.q: What is one advantage of instrumental methods such as flame emission spectroscopy?
options: They are fast, accurate and use very small samples
questions.explain: Instrumental methods like flame emission spectroscopy are fast, accurate and sensitive, working on tiny samples.
